text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Malaysian government has written off arrears on sewerage charges owed by users to the privately-run Indah Water Konsortium (IWK), Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad announced.

-- The managing director of stock exchange listed Kim Hin Industries Bhd, Chua Seng Huat, has been charged in court by the Securities Commission with two counts of insider trading in the first such case in the country.

-- Feedmillers and livestock farmers have been directed by the Health Minister to destroy or export their stocks of drug nitrofuran or risk prosecution. He said the government had quarantined over 41 tonnes of the drug since August 21, when the use of nitrofuran was banned due to fear that it could cause cancer to consumers.

-- Most of Malaysia's automated teller machines (ATM) have been integrated into a common network following a link up between the two main systems, the Malaysia Electronic Payment System and Group Electronic Automated Teller System.
-- Malaysian National Reinsurance Bhd made an impressive debut on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, earning a premium of 3.20 ringgit over the offer price of 4.30.

-- Malaysia Airlines chairman Tajudin Ramli said he has not bid for any government assets in Cook Islands in the South Pacific as they did not fit into his business plans. He was denying a recent wire report which said he was planning to buy assets worth $70.6 million.
-- Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd announced it will buy 19.05 percent stake in Rashid Hussain Bhd for 1.04 billion ringgit.

-- Malaysia's central bank, Bank Negara, is still waiting for an application from Bank of China. The Chinese bank has sought to set up a branch in Malaysia and expects to have one by the middle of next year.
